agent_summary:
Scope: juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop) answers on http only (https:443 refused). Worked lane 87 (Error handling), both items DONE.

WSTG-ERRH-01 (improper error handling) and WSTG-ERRH-02 (stack traces) — confirmed, with evidence:
- JSON error disclosure: GET /rest/products/search?q=test') with Accept: application/json returns 500 JSON leaking error.message, error.stack, code SQLITE_ERROR and the full backend SQL statement (x9). SQLi variants reproduce (x38/x81).
- Full Node stack trace with absolute paths/line numbers: GET /redirect (missing 'to') returns 500 JSON with a TypeError stack listing /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:157, /juice-shop/build/routes/redirect.js:47, verify.js, and node_modules/express internals (x15).
- HTML error template leaks framework/version "OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.22.1)" on 401/500 (x4, x7); GET /profile populates the #stacktrace list with userProfile.js:69 and discloses an internal container IP ::ffff:172.25.0.2 (x28).
- Several benign GETs return unhandled 500s: /rest/country-mapping (x39/x42), /dataerasure (x55 html, x103 json), /rest/chatbot/status (x58), /rest/basket and /rest/track-order with no id (x110/x112).
- Contrast/non-vuln cases: clean 404 JSON for missing resources (/api/Products/99999, /api/Users/abc), unmatched routes fall through to the SPA index 200 (catch-all), and malformed JWT / type-confusion params handled gracefully (x27, x52). So leakage is specific to thrown/unhandled exceptions.

Coverage: ~60 distinct endpoints probed (REST + /api/* models) as anonymous and as test accounts errh1/errh2, including auth-required endpoints returning proper 401/403 (e.g. /rest/order-history/orders, /api/SecurityAnswers, /api/Quantitys/:id) — showing the access-control gaps found are specific, not blanket.

Leads recorded for other lanes (need validation): (HIGH) /api/Users list and /api/Users/:id and /rest/user/authentication-details/ return all users' data to any authenticated customer; /rest/memories exposes other users' password hashes; poison-null-byte /ftp/..%2500.md downloads restricted backups (package.json.bak with JWT secret). (MEDIUM) basket IDOR /rest/basket/{1,2,3} across accounts; exposed directory listings /ftp, /support/logs. (LOW) /encryptionkeys listing, unauth /metrics, customer-readable /api/Quantitys list, wildcard CORS.

Nothing left open. No writes were needed (all tests were achievable read-only); write proposals were therefore not used. Bodies stopped displaying mid-run once the display budget was exhausted, but full responses are retained as evidence (exchange ids cited) and status/length/redaction markers supported the later findings.

leads.title: [agent] /rest/memories exposes other users' account records including password hashes

detail.text: Unauthenticated GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/memories/ returns a list of photo-wall memories that embeds the full User object for each author, including email, password hash, deluxeToken, role (admin/deluxe), isActive and profile image path (e.g. user id 4 username bkimminich role admin). Sensitive account data of other users is exposed without authorization. Belongs to a data-exposure/authorization lane.

leads.title: [agent] Broken access control: /api/Users list returns all users to any authenticated customer

detail.text: Unauthenticated GET /api/Users returns 401 (x7), but signed in as test customer errh1 (and again as errh2) GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users returned HTTP 200 with an ~11KB JSON body; the gateway redacted 38 distinct email addresses, indicating the full Users table is returned to a low-privileged customer. Combined with GET /api/Users/:id (x72) and /rest/user/authentication-details/ (x78/x108), customer accounts can enumerate and read all users' data. High-impact BOLA/BFLA for an authorization lane. Full response retained as evidence x111.

leads.title: [agent] Broken access control: /rest/user/authentication-details/ returns all users' auth details to any customer

detail.text: Signed in as test customer errh1, GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/user/authentication-details/ returned HTTP 200 with a 14540-byte JSON body; the gateway redacted 38 distinct email addresses from it, indicating the response enumerates authentication details for all users rather than only the caller's. Unauthenticated the same endpoint returns 401 (x16), so authentication is required but authorization is not scoped to the caller. Full response retained as evidence x78. High-impact user-data exposure for an authorization lane to validate.

leads.title: [agent] Broken access control: any authenticated customer can read arbitrary user records via /api/Users/:id

detail.text: Signed in as test customer errh1 (id 27), GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Users/1 returned HTTP 200 with a 301-byte JSON body containing another user's record (the gateway flagged one email address in the body). This lets a low-privileged customer enumerate other users (including admin id 1) and read their profile fields. Body not displayed due to budget; full response retained as evidence x72. For an authorization lane to validate.

leads.title: [agent] Customer account can read /api/Quantitys (product stock quantities)

detail.text: Signed in as test customer errh1, GET http://juice.lab.test/api/Quantitys returned HTTP 200 with a 7628-byte JSON body. The Quantitys resource (inventory limits/stock) is intended for admin/accounting roles; a plain customer reading it is a broken-access-control signal. Body not displayed due to budget; full response retained as evidence x40. For an authorization lane to validate.

GET http://juice.lab.test/encryptionkeys/ returns HTTP 200 with a 7958-byte text/html directory listing (same indexing behaviour as /ftp), exposing the application's encryption key files directory to anonymous users. Information-disclosure finding for a dedicated lane. Full body retained as evidence x85.

leads.title: [agent] Exposed /ftp directory listing with sensitive backup files

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp returns a browsable directory listing of 11 entries including package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx (KeePass DB), announcement_encrypted.md, encrypt.pyc and suspicious_errors.yml. Directory indexing plus backup/credential files is an information-disclosure finding for a dedicated lane.

GET http://juice.lab.test/support/logs/ returns HTTP 200 with an 8927-byte text/html directory listing (same indexing as /ftp and /encryptionkeys), exposing server log files to anonymous users. Log files can contain sensitive request data. Information-disclosure finding for a dedicated lane; full body retained as evidence x89.

leads.title: [agent] Poison null byte lets anonymous users download restricted /ftp backup files (package.json.bak with secrets)

detail.text: The /ftp download route only permits .md/.pdf files, but GET http://juice.lab.test/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (an encoded %00 null byte before a .md suffix) returned HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, content-length 4263 — exactly the size of package.json.bak from the /ftp listing. The gateway redacted a jsonwebtoken value and an email address from the body, confirming it contains sensitive data (hardcoded JWT secret, maintainer email). Any anonymous user can retrieve forbidden backup files (and likely other sensitive /ftp entries, e.g. incident-support.kdbx, coupons_2013.md.bak) this way. Path-traversal/file-disclosure finding; full response retained as evidence x121.

leads.title: [agent] Possible IDOR: customer account can fetch another user's basket (/rest/basket/1)

detail.text: Signed in as test account errh1 (a newly registered customer, id 27), GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/basket/1 returned HTTP 200 with a 1310-byte JSON body (content-length 1310), i.e. basket id 1 which is not errh1's own basket. Strong signal of insecure direct object reference on basket retrieval. Body not re-read here due to display budget; full response retained as evidence x34. Belongs to an authorization/IDOR lane for validation.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics endpoint exposes internal process/runtime metrics

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/metrics returns 200 text/plain Prometheus metrics with no auth, disclosing process memory (process_resident_memory_bytes), open FDs, CPU time, event-loop lag, startup task timings, and HTTP status-code counters. Useful to an attacker for fingerprinting/monitoring the backend. Belongs to an information-disclosure/config lane.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/this-path-does-not-exist-12345 -> 200. Characterised 404/not-found handling: unmatched GET paths (e.g. /this-path-does-not-exist-12345, even with Accept: application/json) return HTTP 200 with the SPA index.html (catch-all), while REST endpoints with a missing resource (/api/Products/99999) return a clean 404 JSON {"message":"Not Found","errors":[]} with no internal detail. The verbose leakage is limited to thrown/unhandled errors, not ordinary not-found cases.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/profile -> 500. GET /profile returned a 500 HTML error page (the "OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.22.1)" template) whose #stacktrace list was populated with a server source path and line number (at /juice-shop/build/routes/userProfile.js:69:18) and the error text disclosed an internal container IP (::ffff:172.25.0.2). Confirms stack-trace/internal-path disclosure in the HTML error template as well as the JSON one.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/user/whoami -> 200. Not every bad input leaks: a malformed Authorization bearer token to /rest/user/whoami was handled gracefully, returning 200 {"user":{}} with no error detail. Shows the leakage is specific to unhandled exceptions rather than all error paths. [1 value redacted: Authorization]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/country-mapping -> 500. A plain GET /rest/country-mapping (normally a 200 config response) returned HTTP 500 with a chunked body and no content-type, i.e. an unhandled server error surfaced to the client on a benign request. Full body retained as evidence.
